title: One Point in It at Quinta da Ria
title_candidates: One Point in It at Quinta da Ria
TEG 19 Opens in the Eastern Algarve
Nine at the Tenth, Thirty-Nine for Jon Baker
theme: A new course nobody had seen before, a tenth hole that ruined three cards, and a Trophy lead that changed hands four times before the last green.
opening_hook: TEG 19 began on a Saturday at Quinta da Ria, 12km from Tavira and new to every man in the field, and the Trophy lead changed hands four times between the 5th and the 18th before Jon Baker parred the last to take it by a single point.

round_story.subject: Jon Baker's 39 points, the best score of the opening day, salvaged from a three-hole wobble at the 8th, 9th and 10th
round_story.why_it_matters: It is the highest Stableford score of the round and it puts Jon Baker at the top of the TEG 19 Trophy after day one, on a course playing 1.6 shots harder than the average TEG venue and seen by nobody in the field before Saturday morning.
round_story.shape: Jon Baker was at or near the front from the 4th, where a par took him clear. He then dropped seven gross shots across the 8th, 9th and 10th, doubles at both par fours and a triple at the long 10th, and stood third after the 17th. Three straight pars from the 11th steadied him, and a par at the 18th, worth four points on stroke index 3, took the lead back on the last green.
headline_candidates: Jon Baker Posts Thirty-Nine at Quinta da Ria
Jon Baker Recovers for Thirty-Nine Points
A Par at the Last for Jon Baker
round_story.chosen_headline: Jon Baker Posts Thirty-Nine at Quinta da Ria
round_story.standfirst: Seven gross shots went in three holes around the turn, and he still finished 90 on a course none of the five had played before.

race_story.subject: Alex Baker led the Trophy standing on the 18th tee and finished a point short, while Gregg Williams's 87 opened a three-shot Green Jacket lead
race_story.why_it_matters: Three of the five are within a point of each other in the TEG 19 Trophy, the Green Jacket already has a clear leader, and the Wooden Spoon is shared, so almost nothing is settled going into Sunday.
race_story.shape: Alex Baker went to the front at the 5th with a par worth four points, having taken 13 points from the 3rd to the 6th, then gave away ten gross shots across the 10th, 11th and 12th, including a nine at the 10th. He drew level again at the 14th and led outright after a par at the 17th. He signed for 38, one behind, level with Gregg Williams, whose 87 gross leads the Green Jacket by three from Jon Baker.
headline_candidates: Alex Baker Leads With One Hole Left
A Point Between Three Men After Saturday
Gregg Williams Takes the Green Jacket Lead
race_story.chosen_headline: Alex Baker Leads With One Hole Left
race_story.standfirst: Gregg Williams matched his 38 points and went three clear in the gross with an 87, and David Mullin and John Patterson share the bottom on 31 apiece.

discovered_storylines.subject: The 10th at Quinta da Ria, a 462-yard par four with water and out of bounds, took a nine, an eight and a seven from the field
discovered_storylines.why_it_matters: Three of the five players lost their round's worst hole at the same place on their first ever visit, and two of the three races moved there.
discovered_storylines.shape: Alex Baker went first with a nine, five over par and no points on stroke index 1. David Mullin followed with an eight, which dropped him to the bottom of the Wooden Spoon race, and Jon Baker took a seven as the last of three dropped holes. None of the three had seen the hole before Saturday.
headline_candidates: Nine, Eight and Seven at the Tenth
The Tenth Collects a Nine and an Eight
Three Cards Damaged at the Same Hole
discovered_storylines.chosen_headline: Nine, Eight and Seven at the Tenth
discovered_storylines.standfirst: Out of bounds runs the whole left side and a lake sits in front of the green from 110 yards, which the field discovered one at a time.

discovered_storylines.subject: John Patterson's 105, built from two nines and a ruinous finish, with the best four-hole scoring run of the day in the middle of it
discovered_storylines.why_it_matters: He took the day's worst gross score and still finished level with David Mullin on 31 points at the bottom of the TEG 19 Trophy, so the Wooden Spoon starts the week shared.
discovered_storylines.shape: John Patterson dropped ten shots across the 5th, 6th and 7th, the last of them a nine at the stroke index 2 par four. He then took 12 points from the 8th to the 11th, three apiece, the best four-hole run anyone managed all day. A second nine at the 14th and triples at the 15th and 16th cost him 11 shots in three holes and put him back on the floor of the Spoon race.
headline_candidates: John Patterson's Two Nines and Twelve Points
Twelve Points, Then Eleven Shots Gone
John Patterson Takes Nine Twice on Saturday
discovered_storylines.chosen_headline: John Patterson's Two Nines and Twelve Points
discovered_storylines.standfirst: The 14th doglegs around a lake and the 16th runs between the two biggest ones, and he found both of them expensive.

race_state_note: Three rounds remain. David Mullin and John Patterson are exactly level on 31 points at the foot of the Trophy, so the Spoon is shared rather than owned; Gregg Williams sits second on Stableford and first on gross, three clear of Jon Baker in the Jacket.
